federal.why: FY2024 federal appropriation share of the hundred held constant to FY2030 (D-10, D-11), plus the FY2030 Vaccines for Children purchase, which is wholly federal and peels before the blend (D-71). Derived backward from the hundred: 64.5274 of the hundred is federal once the state residual of 35.4726 is taken, and the 0.7619 vaccine peel is added on top, so 65.2893 enters and 100.0000 is budgeted (D-70). Deriving it forward from the FY2024 federal dollar total instead gives 65.2893, which carries the FY2024 vaccine purchase onto the FY2030 panel and leaves 100.0000 at the agency. Corrected 2026-09-19, D-76.

fig.why: FY2024 federal appropriation share of the hundred held constant to FY2030 (D-10, D-11), plus the FY2030 Vaccines for Children purchase, which is wholly federal and peels before the blend (D-71). Derived backward from the hundred: 64.5274 of the hundred is federal once the state residual of 35.4726 is taken, and the 0.7619 vaccine peel is added on top, so 65.2893 enters and 100.0000 is budgeted (D-70). Deriving it forward from the FY2024 federal dollar total instead gives 65.2893, which carries the FY2024 vaccine purchase onto the FY2030 panel and leaves 100.0000 at the agency. Corrected 2026-09-19, D-76.

Derived backward from the hundred: 64.5274 of the hundred is federal once the state residual of 35.4726 is taken, and the 0.7619 vaccine peel is added on top, so 65.2893 enters and 100.0000 is budgeted (D-70). Deriving it forward from the FY2024 federal dollar total instead gives 65.2893, which carries the FY2024 vaccine purchase onto the FY2030 panel and leaves 100.0000 at the agency. Corrected 2026-09-19, D-76.

fig.why: FY2024 federal appropriation share of the hundred held constant to FY2030 (D-10, D-11), plus the FY2030 Vaccines for Children purchase, which is wholly federal and peels before the blend (D-71). Derived backward from the hundred: 64.5274 of the hundred is federal once the state residual of 35.4726 is taken, and the 0.7619 vaccine peel is added on top, so 65.2893 enters and 100.0000 is budgeted (D-70). Deriving it forward from the FY2024 federal dollar total instead gives 65.2893, which carries the FY2024 vaccine purchase onto the FY2030 panel and leaves 100.0000 at the agency. Corrected 2026-09-19, D-76.

federal.why: FY2024 federal appropriation share of the hundred held constant to FY2030 (D-10, D-11), plus the FY2030 Vaccines for Children purchase, which is wholly federal and peels before the blend (D-71). Derived backward from the hundred: 64.5274 of the hundred is federal once the state residual of 35.4726 is taken, and the 0.7619 vaccine peel is added on top, so 65.2893 enters and 100.0000 is budgeted (D-70). Deriving it forward from the FY2024 federal dollar total instead gives 65.2893, which carries the FY2024 vaccine purchase onto the FY2030 panel and leaves 100.0000 at the agency. Corrected 2026-09-19, D-76.

fig.why: FY2024 federal appropriation share of the hundred held constant to FY2030 (D-10, D-11), plus the FY2030 Vaccines for Children purchase, which is wholly federal and peels before the blend (D-71). Derived backward from the hundred: 64.5274 of the hundred is federal once the state residual of 35.4726 is taken, and the 0.7619 vaccine peel is added on top, so 65.2893 enters and 100.0000 is budgeted (D-70). Deriving it forward from the FY2024 federal dollar total instead gives 65.2893, which carries the FY2024 vaccine purchase onto the FY2030 panel and leaves 100.0000 at the agency. Corrected 2026-09-19, D-76.

amerihealth, wellpoint, medstar: administration and margin are taken from each plan's own CY2024 Title XIX reporting. Margin is a residual — premium less care less administration — because nothing publishes a plan's Medicaid margin directly.

MIXED VINTAGE ON THIS PLATE. Three plans are CY2024 and HSCSN is CY2023. HSCSN predates the managed care regulations and is not an MCO in the regulatory sense, so it files no comparable annual statement and has no Title XIX column to read. It reports to DHCF; that figure has not been acquired. CY2023 stands in, and this plan is therefore a year behind the other three.

The plans are scaled to the CMS-64 managed-care lane. A plan's annual statement and the CMS-64 are different accountings on different year boundaries, and the statements carry locally funded Alliance and ICP money that is outside this hundred. Scaling preserves each plan's share and keeps the lane total the measured one.

MedStar Family Choice, Inc. is not a DC-only entity: it writes $920.1M of Title XIX across two jurisdictions, $545.0M of it in Maryland. Its District figure is Schedule T, not its Title XIX column, and its expenses are apportioned by DC's share of Title XIX premium.
united, pace: retention split not published.
Behavioral health is not a separate node. The DC source folds it into wrap-around services and into the capitated lump.
Beneficiary shares: no matrix built. MACStats Exhibit 21 carries a state dimension and is the route in.

facts.body:
Of every $100 of Medicaid spending, $86.92 arrives as a health service today. Under P.L. 119-21 that becomes $78.36. The rest runs the program: state and plan administration, Medicare premiums returned to the federal government, retained earnings, and a small amount of documented fraud.

Everyone in Medicaid has heard the national number. None of it tells you what happens at your own position in the ecosystem. This deck does, in one currency: dollars per $100.
facts.note: Every figure is read from the model at build time. The ledger conserves to the cent in both years.

facts.kicker: Section 2 · The baseline, before the law
facts.hero: $13.08 runs the program — $5.65 of it through plans.
facts.body:
Before P.L. 119-21 does anything, this is the hundred a plan already works inside. State and program administration takes $7.27. Plan administration and earnings is $5.65. Documented fraud is $0.15.

This is the starting position every provision in the next eight slides is applied to.
facts.note: FY2024 actuals. CMS-64 national totals and MACPAC MACStats, February 2026.

facts.kicker: Section 3 · The national baseline, end to end
facts.hero: $51.34 of every $100 arrives through a plan.
facts.body:
Of the $92.73 a state agency disburses, $40.37 is managed care capitation and $10.97 is dual-plan capitation. The remaining $41.39 is fee for service, which passes the payer phase untouched because no plan holds it.

A capitated dollar is committed the day the month starts. A fee-for-service dollar is committed only when a claim is filed. That is why an enrollment change and a rate change do not feel the same.
facts.note: Dual-plan capitation is carved out because the plans are different, the populations are more expensive, and the law treats them differently.

facts.kicker: Section 4 · The hundred under the law
facts.hero: $6.91 of the $10.07 leaves before a claim exists.
facts.body:
Seven provisions remove $10.07 per $100 by FY2030. Where each one leaves decides who can do anything about it.

$6.91 goes before a claim exists — membership and budget, with nothing to negotiate. $2.10 leaves at the claim, which is what a provider's accounts receivable sees first. $1.07 leaves after the claim, onto a household.
facts.note: Measured at FY2030, where 62.6 percent of the ten-year effect is at full force and every provision has started. FY2030 will not be the worst year.

facts.hero: Work reporting is 40% of the law.
facts.body:
The seven provisions, sorted by size. Work reporting alone is $3.98 of the $10.07 — more than the next two together — and it lands at disbursements, before a claim is ever filed.

Each provision leaves at its own phase for its own reason. Work reporting hits when a state stops disbursing for people who lose coverage to paperwork. Directed payment caps hit only after a claim is filed, which is why they land on a provider's books rather than a state's budget.
facts.note: Plain-language names lead. Section numbers appear parenthetically at first use in the white paper.

facts.body:
No provision in P.L. 119-21 addresses managed care directly. Premium falls 8.38 percent because fewer people are enrolled. Plan administration falls with it, from $4.89 to $4.48, because load sits inside the capitation rate as a percentage of premium. A smaller base yields a smaller administrative dollar with nothing negotiated between payers and states.

Network management, rate setting and regulatory reporting do not shrink because membership does. Risk pool mix will shift, because eligibility rules remove the members easiest to disenroll, not the members most expensive to cover.

The claims phase is different in kind. Under prior law no money left at claims. Under P.L. 119-21, $2.10 leaves here — the only money in the lifecycle removed after the point where a service could already have been rendered.
facts.note: Where a plan holds directed payment arrangements the cap is an instruction to carry out, but the plan rather than the state has to renegotiate with providers.

facts.hero: Three services fall faster because §71116 names them.
facts.body:
Long-term care, hospitals, and physicians and clinics carry the directed payment cap on top of the general contraction, in proportion to how much of each service arrives through a directed payment.

Wrap around services, behavioral health and prescription drugs fall at 8.38 percent. Three services landing on an identical rate to two decimals is the absence of an explanation, not the presence of one.

The rate is a national average. Actual exposure depends on a state's expansion status, its managed care penetration, and an organization's own payer mix and directed payment position. Two hospitals in neighboring states can face materially different outcomes from the same statute.
facts.note: The six services sum to claims paid: $87.07 in FY2024 and $78.50 in FY2030.

facts.hero:
The new adult group carries most of the loss.
Dual eligibles are left holding an unpaid bill.
facts.body:
Nothing else in the law is concentrated like this. §71119 and §71107 name the population enrolled under §1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(VIII) and reach no other, which is why this category moves by more than a quarter while every other category moves by less than five percent.

Of the seven provisions, six reduce what somebody is paid. One converts a Medicaid payment into a household obligation — the clearest statement in the ledger of what “removed from Medicaid” can mean.
facts.note: Coverage is somebody dropped and the whole of their care goes to zero. Rate is the same person, still enrolled, with their provider paid less. No individual loses a share of their own care.

facts.hero: A national average is not a local condition.
facts.note: Corrections and challenges are welcome and will be answered in print.
